limits: A valid receipt says each party’s key signed its own part and the parts chain. It does not say any party told the truth.

The carried keys are the parties’ only if the verifier already holds those key_ids from somewhere else. A receipt cannot vouch for its own keys. When two roles are signed by one key, one holder signed both.
The acceptance names who accepted. The signature proves the acceptor’s key signed the receipt, not that the person named did.
money none means no money is held or paid by this receipt.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a receipt that still verifies.
The checks prove only what they test. A passed record says the pinned commands exited 0 on that tree, not that the work is good.
A test that cannot fail is not detected by this record.

The checker ran them as recorded only as far as the verifier trusts the checker’s key. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued the record, and content_hash that it was not edited since; the carried key is the checker’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a record that still verifies.
A delivery says what the doer’s Tick recorded handing in, not that the work is right. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
cents marked reported came from the agent’s platform and were not measured.
It does not prove the order exists or that this delivery answers it; that is checked where a receipt binds the two.
The carried key is the doer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A delivery cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a delivery that still verifies.
A work order says what was asked, not that anything was done. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
The carried key is the buyer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A work order cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a work order that still verifies.
payment none means no money is held for this order.

WHAT HAPPENED, AND WHAT THE LAST TASK FOUND (2026-10-28, run 01a182f7-072d-77e8-9b3f-d798a3172c1b). tick_status said 'Task "Put it in place, once accepted" is running but no lease holds it, so nobody works it' about a landing step whose one attempt was alive and landed. Task 01a182fa-f147-7772-becb-a90987aab683 read the code and reported no_change_required with this evidence: a plain tick_work stop keeps renewing a held attempt's lease (runner/src/daemon.ts awaits its in-flight attempts before cancelling renewal; the machine's batched renewal, runner/src/machine-connection.ts, runs until the connection closes), so nothing lapsed. The line was wrong because `stranded` (packages/cli/src/project-line.ts, about line 187) tests `task.lease === null`, and the task list's `lease` is never filled (RuntimeNode.lease is set to null in dag/src/materialize.ts and amend.ts and never set otherwise), so it is always null; the only live signal is `working`, from workingOn (packages/api/src/run-task-list.ts, about lines 26-37), which is set only when the coordinator holds the run and has a lease for the task in memory (views/src/task-list.ts documents it absent "when the coordinator does not hold the run"). While the coordinator was waiting to start again on a newer release, a live step showed `running` with no `working`. This task replaces that one's failed land step, 01a182fa-f147-7772-becb-b1f235468b86.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. The run's task list says whether the coordinator holds the run as it answers (a field beside the tasks, e.g. `held: true|false`, set in run-task-list.ts where workingOn is computed, typed and documented in packages/views/src/task-list.ts). An older coordinator that sends no such field is read as not saying.
2. `stranded` names a task only when the list says the coordinator holds the run and the task is `running` with no `working`; where the list says it does not hold the run, or does not say, no task is called stranded (the line says nothing rather than something false). Stop relying on `lease`, which is never filled: leave the field where it is, and say in a one-line comment where it is read that it is not filled.
3. Tests in a new file, packages/cli/src/project-line-held.test.ts: a running task with no working in a list the coordinator holds is stranded; the same in a list it does not hold, or one without the field, is not; a running task with working is never stranded. packages/cli/src/project-line.test.ts is 495 lines: its case at about line 101 expects a single read to name a stranded task; make its fixture say the coordinator holds the run, by changing values in place, and add no line. Read packages/api's tests of handleListRunTasks and run-task-list, and grep the whole tree's *.test.ts for `stranded`, workingOn and ListRunTasksBody fixtures before you finish; every existing assertion keeps passing. If another file must change, ask for it with tick_widen; never weaken or delete a test.

DONE WHEN. Tick's check passes on your commit (call tick_check; do not install, build or run suites in your copy).
